business_summary.text: BirlaNu Limited is a construction materials company with segments in Roofs, Walls, Pipes, Construction Chemicals, and Parador (Europe).

call_points.text: Management expects to continue the momentum of the last two quarters and beat internal targets for FY27.
Parador's order book is healthy, up over 10% YoY, with a strong recovery expected in H2FY27.
BCG cost-out program for Parador expected to deliver 300-400 bps EBITDA uplift by Q4FY27.
Debt-to-equity ratio as of 30th June is 0.68x, which is within manageable range.
PVC pipe segment faces transient challenges due to price volatility, but government measures are expected to stabilize prices.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: With respect to the demand notice for an amount of Rs. 71.60 crore in HSN Classification code case, Appellate Authority confirmed the demand of Rs.71.60 crore by not considering the arguments made by the Company during the hearings. Aggrieved by the same, the Company challenged the appeal orders in High Court of Madras by filing Writ Petitions for the period from 2017-18 to 2022. The matter was heard by the Court in July 2025. With respect to the notice for an amount of Rs. 4.70 crore for balance period of FY 23 (Sep'22 - Mar'23), the Company submitted its reply to the Asst. Commissioner, Madhavaram Circle, Chennai and also attended personal hearing on 10.05.2024 and argued on the matter by submitting addl. grounds and awaiting orders in this regard. Meanwhile, pursuant to the decisions taken in the 55th GST Council Meeting, the CBIC, vide Circular No. 247/25/2025-GST dated 14.02.2025, has clarified that AAC Blocks containing more than 50% Fly Ash shall be classified under HSN Code 6815 and shall attract GST at the rate of 12%. In light of the above clarification, Company had filed Miscellaneous Writ Petition (MWP) before Madras High Court and received a favourable order dated July 14, 2025 with a direction to file the application for claiming refund of Rs. 2 crore, alongwith interest, which was paid under protest. Accordingly, the Company submitted the applications with the concerned GST Authorities for the refund of amount of Rs. 4.94 crore, (Rs. 2 crore paid under protest and appeal admission tax of Rs. 2.94 crore) alongwith interest of Rs. 86.53 lakh. In response to the said applications, the Company has received refund of Rs. 2.59 crore along with interest of Rs. 43.58 lakh during the month of September 2025. Further, the refund of balance amount of Rs. 2.35 crore along with interest of Rs. 42.95 lakh is expected to be received in the month of October 2025.
tax_litigation.status: The Company was contesting a GST demand of INR 71.60 crore (FY 17-18 to FY 22-23 up to Aug’22) before the Hon’ble Madras High Court in the HSN classification code case. Another demand of INR 4.70 crore, (FY 22-23 Sep-Mar) on the same issue was at adjudication stage. Subsequent to CBIC clarification (during Feb’25), classifying AAC Blocks with >50% of Fly Ash content under HSN Code of 6815 attracts 12% of Rate of GST supported Company’s position. Pursuant to CBIC clarification, the Company obtained a favourable order from the Hon’ble Madras High Court permitting refund of amount paid under protest along with amount paid as pre-deposit for admission of appeals. Company applied for refund of INR 4.94 crore, along with interest of INR 86.53 lakh and has received the entire refund in two tranches, INR 2.59 crore, (with interest of INR 43.58 lakh) was received in September’25 and the balance amount of INR 2.35 crore, (with interest of INR 42.95 lakh) was received in October’25. Company is in process of coordinating with the GST Dept., for obtaining Final Asst. Order for the balance period of FY 2022-23 (from September’22 to March’23).

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company received an order from the Office of the Joint Commissioner of State Tax, Patna Special Circle under Section 73(9) of the BGST/CGST Act 2017, read with Section 20 of the IGST Act 2017 with a demand of Rs.685.93 lakhs. This order pertains to disallowance of claim of Input Tax Credit and suppression of purchase turnover arrived on assumption basis and levied tax liability at 18% on above issues specific to the state of Bihar for the financial year 2019-20. The tax liability is calculated by enhancing the taxable turnover and disallowance of claim of GST Credit for the said year. Following the receipt of the assessment order, the Company filed an appeal before Addl. Commissioner (Appeals), Patna on 15.11.2024 by depositing Rs. 36.78 lakh and attended hearings held in this regard. The Company further submitted additional grounds along with relevant supporting information to strengthen its contention. Pursuant to the said appeal, the Company received the Appellate order on May 21, 2025 wherein the appellate authority partially reduced the tax demand but rejected the Company's position and confirmed the suppression of purchase turnover (which was arrived at on the assumption basis) along with other disallowances. Vide said order dated May 21, 2025, the demand has been reduced to Rs. 672.56 lakh (Tax: Rs. 360.62 lakh plus Rs. 275.87 lakh interest and Rs. 36.06 lakh penalty) from Rs. 698.93 Lakh (Tax: Rs. 367.79 lakh plus Rs. 281.36 lakh interest and Rs. 36.78 lakh penalty). Aggrieved by the Appellate order dated on May 21, 2025, the Company has decided to challenge the said Appeal Order before GST Appellate Tribunal (which is under formation) by making payment of additional 10%-20% of tax portion to obtain Stay till the filing of 2nd stage of appeal. There is no update in the matter in Q2FY26.

watchlist.response: I am not 100% sure of which peers you are talking about, but I would request you to also just try and do a deeper analysis of the peer results because a lot of our peers have in the last 3 or 4 years, added boards in their portfolio and the numbers that get reported are a consolidation of boards and Roofing, whereas the Roofing numbers you are talking for us are pure-play Roofing numbers, and we have not sort of consolidated those with our boards number.
